Below are several examples of how the direct interface mode would 
 work in a real-world environment. Note that these are only basic examples, 
 and that your business needs might require a scenario that is not outlined 
 in this topic. Talk to your Manhattan representative for any specific 
 questions that might arise from these examples.
The following is discussed in this topic:

Downloading New Order Header, Detail, 
 Nested Containers, & Comments on the Header and the Detail

Downloading a Delete/Change Action for 
 a Order Header & Detail

Downloading a Delete/Change Action for 
 a Order Detail Only

Downloading a New Receipt Header, Detail, 
 & Container

 Receipt Header & Detail

Order Touchpoint - Downloading 
 New Order Header, Detail, Nested Containers, & Comments on the Header 
 and the Detail

This 
 scenario describes the type of records that you would download in a typical 
 outbound flow. Also, this example includes such complexities as nested 
 containers and comments on the header and the detail. The database value 
 list below represents a full order taken from the ERP system, complete 
 with basic customer/shipping data (header), item data (detail), container 
 data, and additional order comments. Downloading this data would result 
 in a completely new shipment being created in SCALE.

New shipments (orders) 
 can enter the application in several areas. For example, you could have 
 new orders enter into the system with a status of Packing Pending (they would then be available to 
 be packed). Or, you could choose to have them enter into the pool with a status of In Pool (they would then be available 
 to be added to a wave).

: 
 When downloading new order headers, the interface system value "Interface 
 Shipment New Status" identifies the status that the system will assign 
 to the new shipment when it enters SCALE.

: When interfacing 
 a container with a header/detail, you need to tie the container to the       header using the Interface Link 
 ID value. In the above example, since the container also includes an item 
 quantity, the container must tie back to the detail using the ERP Order 
 Line Number value.

: You 
 need to provide this value in order to indicate to SCALE what type of action 
 the system will perform on the data record you will be interfacing (New, 
 Change, Delete, or Save). See the

This value is 
 optional for the detail in this scenario because the Link ID makes the 
 association between the header and the detail.

The Parent 
 Link ID value is not used. Do not provide this value.

To nest 
 a child container in a parent container, you need to link the parent's 
 Interface Record ID to the child's Interface Link ID.

For each item quantity inside a container, you need to provide a "contents 
 record," which actually represents the item quantity. In the example 
 below, the line below the "NESTCONT74334" child container is 
 the contents record for that container. If you do not provide this record, 
 the quantity of the container will be 0, even if you provide a Quantity 
 Field value.

Header comments 
 should be linked to the shipment's Interface Record ID.

Detail comments 
 should be linked to the shipment line's Interface Record ID.

The following is a sample listing of the 
 database values (and the tables they should be on) that need to be present 
 to directly download this type of data.

 Action Code, ERP Order, Warehouse, Shipment

 Address 1, Ship To City, Ship To State, Ship To Postal Code, Ship 
 To Country, Scheduled

 Detail Only

Suppose your ERP functional flow allows you add order lines to an order 
 after it has been interfaced 
 to SCALE. You then would need to download an individual detail record in 
 New mode. This will result in the new line(s) being assigned to the already-existing 
 order.

: This value

 record, therefore you do not need to provide a link ID to associate the 
 detail with the header. The ERP Order value provides this association.

 the system will perform on the data record you will be interfacing (New, 
 Change, Delete, or Save). See the

 to directly download this type of data.

 Code, ERP Order, ERP Order Line Number, Item, Total Qty, Quantity 
 UM, Warehouse, Shipment ID

Order Touchpoint - Downloading a 
 Delete/Change Action for an Order Header & Detail
Suppose a customer wanted to delete or change a detail of an order

it has been interfaced into SCALE. 
 You then would need to download the modified header and/or detail data 
 in Delete or Change mode. This will result in the new data being removed 
 (delete action) or assigned (change action) to the already-existing shipment.

The delete 
 and change actions share the same "required" fields; however, 
 these fields are different than those required for a New Action.

Make sure that the ERP Order Line Number (detail) and Shipment ID (header) 
 correspond to the existing values.

 the system will perform on the data record you will be interfacing (New, 
 Change, Delete, or Save). See the

 to directly download this type of data.       In 
 the example below, the supposition is that you want to change the Carrier 
 Service on the shipment, and the quantity on the shipment line.

 Code, Warehouse,       Shipment ID,

Order Touchpoint - Downloading a 
 Delete/Change Action for an Order Detail Only

Suppose a customer wanted to delete or change a detail of an order after it has been interfaced into SCALE. 
 You then would need to download the detail data in Delete or Change mode. 
 This will result in the new data being removed (delete action) or assigned 
 (change action) to the already-existing shipment

The delete 
 and change actions share the same "required" fields; however, 
 these fields are different than those required for a New Action.

Make sure that the ERP Order Line Number (detail) and Shipment ID (header) 
 correspond to the existing values.

 the system will perform on the data record you will be interfacing (New, 
 Change, Delete, or Save). See the

Need to provide

 header (because there is no link ID).

Downloading Changes to BOM Component 
 Lines

: To download a change to a BOM component line, you will need 
 to download three types of records: one (or more) for the component detail(s) 
 that you want to change (use the Interface Link ID to link back to the 
 finished item); one for the finished item detail that the component is 
 a part of (use the Interface Link ID to link to the shipment that 
 contains this finished item); and one for the shipment. This way, 
 the system has a way to link the component to the finished item, and the 
 finished item to the header. You do not have to make changes to the finished 
 item detail or the header, but they must be included in the download.

Download_Order_Detail: Interface Record ID, Interface Action 
 Code, ERP Order Line Number, Shipment ID, Item, Warehouse

Order Touchpoint - Using Save Actions For 
 Order Downloads

When you run an interface Save action, the system will do one of two 
 things, depending on the status of the data in the system:

- If the data already exists, 
 the system will handle this data record as a Change action.

- If the data does not exist, 
 the system will handle this as a New action.

Receiving Touchpoint - Downloading New 
 Receipt Header, Detail, & Container

This scenario describes 
 the type records that you would download in a typical receiving flow. 
 The data map below represents a full receipt taken from the ERP system, 
 complete with basic vendor data (header), item data (detail), plus additional 
 receipt comments.

New receipts can enter 
 the application in several areas. For example, you could have receipts 
 enter the system with the statuses "Check In Pending" (they 
 would need to be manually checked in via RF or the Receipt Workbench), 
 or "Locate Pending" (bypassing the check-in process, these receipts 
 would need to be located to a location via RF or the Receipt Workbench).

: When 
 downloading new receipt headers, the interface system value "Interface 
 Receipt New Status" identifies the status that the system will assign 
 the new receipt when it enters SCALE.

: This value is 
 optional for the detail in this scenario because the Link ID makes the 
 association between the header and the detail.

: This 
 value relates a receipt container with its detail records. If this value 
 is not specified on the receipt container data map, the system will treat 
 the receipt container as a parent container.

The 
 following is a sample listing of the database values (and the tables they 
 should be on) that need to be present to directly download this type of 
 data.

Download_Receipt_Header: Interface Record ID, Interface 
 Action Code, Receipt ID, 
 Warehouse, Receipt ID Type, ERP Order, Carrier, Carrier Service

Download_Receipt_Detail: Interface Record ID, Interface Link 
 ID, Interface Action Code, Item,       Total Quantity,       ERP 
 Order Line Number, Receipt ID, Quantity UM, Warehouse

Download_Receipt_Container: Interface Record ID, Interface Link 
 ID, Interface Action Code, Quantity, Container ID, Container Type

Inventory Touchpoint - Uploading Inventory Transaction 
 Data

Inventory transactions, such as positive/negative adjustments, can be 
 uploaded to your ERP system. This will ensure that the ERP keeps its inventory 
 balances aligned with the system's totals.

: 
 The "before" on hand quantity value refers to an item quantity 
 that is present in a location before a transaction is performed. The "after" 
 on hand quantity refers to how much of an item after the inventory transaction 
 is performed.
What Data Does The System Upload

The system will upload records for all inventory transactions that have 
 occurred since the interface was last run. The exception to this are transactions 
 that are associated with an adjustment type that is configured not to 
 be included with interface uploads.

Item Touchpoint - Downloading New Item Master 
 Data

SCALE allows you to download 
 item master information from your ERP to the system. This allows you to 
 populate the item master configuration database table, so there is no 
 need to manually define your products in the system.

For example, suppose that 
 your company added a product to their sales inventory. You would then 
 need to create an item master record for this product in SCALE. While this 
 can be done manually via the Configurations Explorer, you can also download 
 this item master data from your ERP.

: The 
 number designation after some of the item values (Weight 1, Quantity UM 
 1, etc) are there to identify the unit of measure definitions for this 
 item (in lieu of creating an item unit of measure record in SCALE). For 
 example, in the above example, each (1) and case (2) unit of measures 
 are being defined for the item. The conversion quantity values determine 
 how many units of an item is in a particular unit of measure (each=1, 
 case=10). The system will take this data and create a record in the Item 
 Unit of Measures Window for this item.

: You cannot interface 
 an item in which the Item ID does not match an existing item template 
 in SCALE (an audit will be generated).
: The item field must be the item defined in the item master. Any item cross references are not looked up by the interface. You can download a cross reference but it is not used.

The following is a sample listing of the 
 database values (and the tables they should be on) that need to be present 
 to directly download this type of data.

Download_Item: Interface Record ID, Interface Action 
 Code, Item, Description, 
 List Price, Conversion Quantity 1, Quantity UM 1, Weight 1, Weight UM 
 1, Conversion Quantity 2, Quantity UM 2, Weight 2, Weight UM 2

Item Touchpoint - Downloading Changes 
 In Item Master Data

Suppose there has been 
 a change to an item's master record in your ERP. You would then need to 
 download this information, in order to reflect this change in the system's 
 item master table. You can use the interface for this change so there 
 is no need to manually update item master records in SCALE.

For example, suppose that 
 one of your company's products changed characteristics (item color, dimensions, 
 price, etc). You would then need to modify this product's item master 
 record in SCALE. While this can be done manually via the Configurations 
 Explorer, you can also download this modified item master data from your 
 ERP.

: The 
 number designation after some of the item values (Weight 1, Quantity UM 
 1, etc) are there to identify the unit of measure definitions for this 
 item (in lieu of creating an item unit of measure record in SCALE). For 
 example, in the above example, each (1) and case (2) unit of measures 
 are being defined for the item. The conversion quantity values determine 
 how many units of an item is in a particular unit of measure (each=1, 
 case=10). The system will take this data and create a record in the Item 
 Unit of Measures Window for this item.

, 
 you only need to have the fields that you want to change present on the 
 data map. The exception is if you want to make unit of measure changes, 
 because you will need to identify on which unit of measure you want to 
 make the change on (in the above example, each UM). The system will make 
 the appropriate changes on the item records and/or item unit of measure 
 records.

: If you download a change and include an item cross reference that the system does not have, it will be added. However, item cross references are not used or looked up by the interface. Only the item defined in the item master is used by the system using an interface.

The following is a sample listing of the 
 database values (and the tables they should be on) that need to be present 
 to directly download this type of data.

Download_Item: Interface Record ID, Interface Action 
 Code, Item, List Price

Item Balance Touchpoint - Uploading Item Balance 
 Data

You can upload item balance 
 information from the system to your ERP. This allows you to reconcile 
 the current item quantities in your warehouse with the ERP's item master 
 table. This is helpful so your ERP has a current and accurate listing 
 of the items in your warehouse and how many are available. In order to 
 gather the item balance data, the system:

- Groups all location inventory 
 records by warehouse, item, company, and inventory status.

- Excludes the records that 
 are associated to a location classes that are not defined to be included 
 in item balance uploads.

- Summarizes the quantity buckets 
 across the remaining records in the group.

- Checks to see if the Include 
 Zero On Hand Items flag is on. If so, then the system cycles through the 
 item master and adds a record for each item/company that is not yet represented 
 in the upload.

- Writes the information to 
 the upload table.

The following is a sample listing of the 
 database values (and the tables they should be on) that need to be present 
 to directly upload this type of data.

Upload_Item_Balance: Interface Record ID, Interface Action 
 Code, Warehouse,       Item, Item 
 Description, On Hand Quantity, Inventory Status

 Receipt Header, Detail, & Container

 optional for the detail in this scenario because the Link ID makes the

 Action Code, Receipt ID,

 1, etc) are there to identify the unit of measure definitions for this 
 item (in lieu of creating an item unit of measure record in SCALE). For

 to directly upload this type of data.

 Code, Warehouse,       Item, Item 
 Description, On Hand Quantity, Inventory Status

 ID value), you can either leave the value blank (as in the example above) 
 or any other valid value. The system will ignore this value as it does 
 not use it to link back to the receipt.

 this value because there is no way to associate this detail with the existing 
 header (because there is no link ID).

The following is a sample listing of the 
 database values (and the tables they should be on) that need to be present 
 to directly download this type of data.

 Code, Item,       Total 
 Quantity,       ERP Order Line Number, 
 Receipt ID, Quantity UM, Warehouse

                    
 

                

            

        

        
 

        
 

        
Receiving Touchpoint - Downloading a 
 Delete/Change Action for an Receipt Header & Detail

        
 

        

            
            
            

                

                    
Functional Scenario

                    
Suppose a customer wanted to delete or change a detail of an receipt 
 after it has been interfaced 
 into SCALE. You then would need to download the modified header and/or detail 
 data in Delete or Change mode. This will result in the new data being 
 removed (delete action) or assigned (change action) to the already-existing 
 receipt.

                    
 

                

                

                    
Field Notes

                    
- Required Fields: The delete 
 and change actions share the same "required" fields; however, 
 these fields are different than those required for a New Action.

                    
 

                    
- ERP Order Line Number/Shipment ID: 
 Make sure that the ERP Order Line Number (detail) and Shipment ID (header) 
 correspond to the existing values.

                    
 

                    
- Interface Action Code: You 
 need to provide this value in order to indicate to SCALE what type of action 
 the system will perform on the data record you will be interfacing (New, 
 Change, Delete, or Save). See the       Direct 
 Mode Overview for more on these actions).

                    
 

                

            

        

        
 

        
Direct Interface Example (Change Action)

        
The following is a sample listing of the 
 database values (and the tables they should be on) that need to be present 
 to directly download this type of data. In 
 the example below, the supposition is that you want to change the Carrier 
 Service on the receipt header, and the Quantity on the receipt detail.

        
 

        
 

        

            
            

                

                    
Download_Order_Header: Interface Record ID, Interface Action 
 Code, Warehouse,       Receipt ID, 
 Carrier Service

                    
 

                

            

            

                

                    
Download_Order_Detail: Interface Record ID, Interface Action 
 Code, Interface Link ID, ERP Order Line Number, Receipt ID, Item, Total Qty, Quantity UM

                    
 

                

            

        

        
 

        
 

        


        
 

        
 

        
 

        
Inventory Touchpoint - Uploading Inventory Transaction 
 Data

        
 

        

            
            
            

                

                    
Functional Scenario

                    
Inventory transactions, such as positive/negative adjustments, can be 
 uploaded to your ERP system. This will ensure that the ERP keeps its inventory 
 balances aligned with the system's totals.

                    
 

                

                

                    
Field Notes

                    
- Before & After On Hand Quantity: 
 The "before" on hand quantity value refers to an item quantity 
 that is present in a location before a transaction is performed. The "after" 
 on hand quantity refers to how much of an item after the inventory transaction 
 is performed.

                    
 

                

            

            

                

                    
What Data Does The System Upload

                    
The system will upload records for all inventory transactions that have 
 occurred since the interface was last run. The exception to this are transactions 
 that are associated with an adjustment type that is configured not to 
 be included with interface uploads.

                

                

                    
 

                    
 

                

            

        

        
 

        
 

        


        
 

        
 

        
Item Touchpoint - Downloading New Item Master 
 Data

        
 

        

            
            
            

                

                    
Functional Scenario

                    
SCALE allows you to download 
 item master information from your ERP to the system. This allows you to 
 populate the item master configuration database table, so there is no 
 need to manually define your products in the system.

                    
 

                    
For example, suppose that 
 your company added a product to their sales inventory. You would then 
 need to create an item master record for this product in SCALE. While this 
 can be done manually via the Configurations Explorer, you can also download 
 this item master data from your ERP.

                    
 

                

                

                    
Field Notes

                    
- Numbered Field Values: The 
 number designation after some of the item values (Weight 1, Quantity UM 
 1, etc) are there to identify the unit of measure definitions for this 
 item (in lieu of creating an item unit of measure record in SCALE). For 
 example, in the above example, each (1) and case (2) unit of measures 
 are being defined for the item. The conversion quantity values determine 
 how many units of an item is in a particular unit of measure (each=1, 
 case=10). The system will take this data and create a record in the Item 
 Unit of Measures Window for this item.

                    
 

                    
- Restriction: You cannot interface 
 an item in which the Item ID does not match an existing item template 
 in SCALE (an audit will be generated).

                    
 

                    
- Item Cross References: The item field must be the item defined in the item master. Any item cross references are not looked up by the interface. You can download a cross reference but it is not used.

                    
 

                

            

        

        
 

        
Direct Interface Example (New Action)

        
The following is a sample listing of the 
 database values (and the tables they should be on) that need to be present 
 to directly download this type of data.

        
 

        

            
            

                

                    
Download_Item: Interface Record ID, Interface Action 
 Code, Item, Description, 
 List Price, Conversion Quantity 1, Quantity UM 1, Weight 1, Weight UM 
 1, Conversion Quantity 2, Quantity UM 2, Weight 2, Weight UM 2

                

            

        

        
 

        
 

        
 

        
Item Touchpoint - Downloading Changes 
 In Item Master Data

        
 

        

            
            
            

                

                    
Functional Scenario

                    
Suppose there has been 
 a change to an item's master record in your ERP. You would then need to 
 download this information, in order to reflect this change in the system's 
 item master table. You can use the interface for this change so there 
 is no need to manually update item master records in SCALE.

                    
 

                    
For example, suppose that 
 one of your company's products changed characteristics (item color, dimensions, 
 price, etc). You would then need to modify this product's item master 
 record in SCALE. While this can be done manually via the Configurations 
 Explorer, you can also download this modified item master data from your 
 ERP.

                    
 

                

                

                    
Field Notes

                    
- Numbered Field Values: The 
 number designation after some of the item values (Weight 1, Quantity UM 
 1, etc) are there to identify the unit of measure definitions for this 
 item (in lieu of creating an item unit of measure record in SCALE). For 
 example, in the above example, each (1) and case (2) unit of measures 
 are being defined for the item. The conversion quantity values determine 
 how many units of an item is in a particular unit of measure (each=1, 
 case=10). The system will take this data and create a record in the Item 
 Unit of Measures Window for this item.

                    
 

                    
- For item master change actions, 
 you only need to have the fields that you want to change present on the 
 data map. The exception is if you want to make unit of measure changes, 
 because you will need to identify on which unit of measure you want to 
 make the change on (in the above example, each UM). The system will make 
 the appropriate changes on the item records and/or item unit of measure 
 records.

                    
 

                    
- Item Cross References: If you download a change and include an item cross reference that the system does not have, it will be added. However, item cross references are not used or looked up by the interface. Only the item defined in the item master is used by the system using an interface.

                    
 

                

            

        

        
 

        
Direct Interface Example (Change Action)

        
The following is a sample listing of the 
 database values (and the tables they should be on) that need to be present 
 to directly download this type of data. 

        
 

        

            
            

                

                    
Download_Item: Interface Record ID, Interface Action 
 Code, Item, List Price

                    
 

                

            

        

        
 

        


        
 

        
 

        
Item Balance Touchpoint - Uploading Item Balance 
 Data

        
 

        

            
            

                

                    
Functional Scenario

                    
You can upload item balance 
 information from the system to your ERP. This allows you to reconcile 
 the current item quantities in your warehouse with the ERP's item master 
 table. This is helpful so your ERP has a current and accurate listing 
 of the items in your warehouse and how many are available. In order to 
 gather the item balance data, the system:

                    
 

                    
- Groups all location inventory 
 records by warehouse, item, company, and inventory status. 

                    
 

                    
- Excludes the records that 
 are associated to a location classes that are not defined to be included 
 in item balance uploads.

                    
 

                    
- Summarizes the quantity buckets 
 across the remaining records in the group.

                    
 

                    
- Checks to see if the Include 
 Zero On Hand Items flag is on. If so, then the system cycles through the 
 item master and adds a record for each item/company that is not yet represented 
 in the upload. 

                    
 

                    
- Writes the information to 
 the upload table.

                    
 

                

            

        

        
 

        
Direct Interface Example

        
The following is a sample listing of the 
 database values (and the tables they should be on) that need to be present 
 to directly upload this type of data. 

        
 

        

            
            

                

                    
Upload_Item_Balance: Interface Record ID, Interface Action 
 Code, Warehouse,       Item, Item 
 Description, On Hand Quantity, Inventory Status

Functional Scenario
                    This 
 scenario describes the type of records that you would download in a typical 
 outbound flow. Also, this example includes such complexities as nested 
 containers and comments on the header and the detail. The database value 
 list below represents a full order taken from the ERP system, complete 
 with basic customer/shipping data (header), item data (detail), container 
 data, and additional order comments. Downloading this data would result

 can enter the application in several areas. For example, you could have 
 new orders enter into the system with a status of Packing Pending (they would then be available to

 When downloading new order headers, the interface system value "Interface 
 Shipment New Status" identifies the status that the system will assign

 Line Number value.

 need to provide this value in order to indicate to SCALE what type of action 
 the system will perform on the data record you will be interfacing (New, 
 Change, Delete, or Save). See the       Direct 
 Mode Overview for more on these actions).

 optional for the detail in this scenario because the Link ID makes the 
 association between the header and the detail.
                     
                    - Parent Link ID: The Parent 
 Link ID value is not used. Do not provide this value.
                     
                    - Nesting Containers: To nest 
 a child container in a parent container, you need to link the parent's 
 Interface Record ID to the child's Interface Link ID.
                     
                    - "Contents" Records: 
 For each item quantity inside a container, you need to provide a "contents 
 record," which actually represents the item quantity. In the example 
 below, the line below the "NESTCONT74334" child container is 
 the contents record for that container. If you do not provide this record, 
 the quantity of the container will be 0, even if you provide a Quantity 
 Field value.
                     
                    - Header Comments: Header comments 
 should be linked to the shipment's Interface Record ID.
                     
                    - Detail Comments: Detail comments 
 should be linked to the shipment line's Interface Record ID.

Functional Scenario
                    Inventory transactions, such as positive/negative adjustments, can be 
 uploaded to your ERP system. This will ensure that the ERP keeps its inventory 
 balances aligned with the system's totals.

Field Notes
                    - Before & After On Hand Quantity: 
 The "before" on hand quantity value refers to an item quantity 
 that is present in a location before a transaction is performed. The "after" 
 on hand quantity refers to how much of an item after the inventory transaction 
 is performed.

What Data Does The System Upload
                    The system will upload records for all inventory transactions that have 
 occurred since the interface was last run. The exception to this are transactions 
 that are associated with an adjustment type that is configured not to 
 be included with interface uploads.

Functional Scenario
                    SCALE allows you to download 
 item master information from your ERP to the system. This allows you to 
 populate the item master configuration database table, so there is no 
 need to manually define your products in the system.
                     
                    For example, suppose that 
 your company added a product to their sales inventory. You would then 
 need to create an item master record for this product in SCALE. While this 
 can be done manually via the Configurations Explorer, you can also download 
 this item master data from your ERP.

Field Notes
                    - Numbered Field Values: The 
 number designation after some of the item values (Weight 1, Quantity UM 
 1, etc) are there to identify the unit of measure definitions for this 
 item (in lieu of creating an item unit of measure record in SCALE). For 
 example, in the above example, each (1) and case (2) unit of measures 
 are being defined for the item. The conversion quantity values determine 
 how many units of an item is in a particular unit of measure (each=1, 
 case=10). The system will take this data and create a record in the Item 
 Unit of Measures Window for this item.
                     
                    - Restriction: You cannot interface 
 an item in which the Item ID does not match an existing item template 
 in SCALE (an audit will be generated).
                     
                    - Item Cross References: The item field must be the item defined in the item master. Any item cross references are not looked up by the interface. You can download a cross reference but it is not used.

Functional Scenario
                    Suppose there has been 
 a change to an item's master record in your ERP. You would then need to 
 download this information, in order to reflect this change in the system's 
 item master table. You can use the interface for this change so there 
 is no need to manually update item master records in SCALE.
                     
                    For example, suppose that 
 one of your company's products changed characteristics (item color, dimensions, 
 price, etc). You would then need to modify this product's item master 
 record in SCALE. While this can be done manually via the Configurations 
 Explorer, you can also download this modified item master data from your 
 ERP.

Field Notes
                    - Numbered Field Values: The 
 number designation after some of the item values (Weight 1, Quantity UM 
 1, etc) are there to identify the unit of measure definitions for this 
 item (in lieu of creating an item unit of measure record in SCALE). For 
 example, in the above example, each (1) and case (2) unit of measures 
 are being defined for the item. The conversion quantity values determine 
 how many units of an item is in a particular unit of measure (each=1, 
 case=10). The system will take this data and create a record in the Item 
 Unit of Measures Window for this item.
                     
                    - For item master change actions, 
 you only need to have the fields that you want to change present on the 
 data map. The exception is if you want to make unit of measure changes, 
 because you will need to identify on which unit of measure you want to 
 make the change on (in the above example, each UM). The system will make 
 the appropriate changes on the item records and/or item unit of measure 
 records.
                     
                    - Item Cross References: If you download a change and include an item cross reference that the system does not have, it will be added. However, item cross references are not used or looked up by the interface. Only the item defined in the item master is used by the system using an interface.

Functional Scenario
                    You can upload item balance 
 information from the system to your ERP. This allows you to reconcile 
 the current item quantities in your warehouse with the ERP's item master 
 table. This is helpful so your ERP has a current and accurate listing 
 of the items in your warehouse and how many are available. In order to 
 gather the item balance data, the system:
                     
                    - Groups all location inventory 
 records by warehouse, item, company, and inventory status. 
                     
                    - Excludes the records that 
 are associated to a location classes that are not defined to be included 
 in item balance uploads.
                     
                    - Summarizes the quantity buckets 
 across the remaining records in the group.
                     
                    - Checks to see if the Include 
 Zero On Hand Items flag is on. If so, then the system cycles through the 
 item master and adds a record for each item/company that is not yet represented 
 in the upload. 
                     
                    - Writes the information to 
 the upload table.
